i18n.en: Then Yosef could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Yosef made himself known unto his brethren.

*Lo yakhol Yosef le-hit'appeq* — 'Yosef could not restrain himself' — is the structural arc-collapse the cycle has been preparing across the chapter-43 → chapter-44 sequence. The central [`yitappaq-emotional-restraint-yosef-arc`](#yitappaq-emotional-restraint-yosef-arc) entry, anchored at Gen 43:31 (where Yosef CAN restrain himself at the stewardship-feast scene), extends here to its antithetical-pair: Yosef CANNOT restrain himself at the disclosure-scene, when Yehudah's surety-speech (Gen 44:18-34) has finally overwhelmed his control. The Hithpael's force is precise: not generic 'be patient' but the active forcing-of-oneself; the lexeme names the breakdown of the self-imposed-restraint. Alter, Sternberg, and Fokkelman name the Gen 43:31 → 45:1 pair as one of the corpus's most concentrated emotional-arc markers.

The chapter's privacy-command — *hotzi'u kol-ish me'alai* ('cause every man to go out from me') — is one of two HB occurrences of this exact audience-clearing formula; the only other is 2 Sam 13:9, Amnon's command before the Tamar-violation. The Gen 45:1 / 2 Sam 13:9 lexical-pair is a documented Alter / Sternberg / Fokkelman literary observation: the formula deploys the verbatim audience-clearing command at the corpus's two most-charged private-encounter-scenes — one a disclosure-of-reconciliation, one a violation. The contrast is part of the corpus's literary-architecture; the construction is preserved without overlay-housing.

*Be-hitvadda Yosef el-echav* — 'while Yosef made himself known unto his brethren' — deploys the marked Hithpael of *yada* (governed by the new overlay [`hitvadda-yosef-self-disclosure-recognition-pair-gen45`](#hitvadda-yosef-self-disclosure-recognition-pair-gen45)) as the disclosure-scene's signature verb. The Hithpael is rare: only one cross-corpus parallel in this specific register, at Num 12:6 (YHWH's *etvadda* — divine-self-disclosure-to-the-prophet). The construction stands as the explicit literary inverse of Gen 42:7's *va-yitnakker* ('made himself strange', the Hithpael of *nakar*, governed by the SIBLING overlay [`nakar-hitnakker-recognition-feigning-gen42`](#nakar-hitnakker-recognition-feigning-gen42)). The cycle's recognition-arc deploys two Hithpael-stems at structurally-opposed moments: *hitnakker* (recognition-withheld at Gen 42:7) → *hitvadda* (recognition-disclosed at Gen 45:1). The pair is the cycle's signature Hithpael-architecture; both rationales cross-reference the other by id.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ בִּבְכִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And he wept aloud: and the Mitsrim heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ אֲנִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף הַע֥וֹד אָבִ֖י חָ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ לַעֲנ֣וֹת אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִבְהֲל֖וּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto his brethren, I am Yosef; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were dismayed at his presence.

paragraphs.commentary:
The cycle's central disclosure-utterance — *ani Yosef ha-od avi chai* ('I am Yosef; doth my father yet live?') — is one of the most-cited verses in the HB for its dramatic force. The terse three-word Hebrew construction has no lexical decision per se; the literary point is the *od-Yosef-chai* refrain that runs across the chapter (v 3 Yosef's self-disclosure; v 26 the brothers' announcement to Ya'aqov; v 28 Ya'aqov's acceptance), one of the chapter's principal declarative-keywords. Alter, Sternberg, and Westermann all name the refrain as the chapter's structuring-formula without lexical-housing.

The brothers' speechlessness — *lo yakhlu echav la-anot oto ki nivhalu mi-panav* ('they could not answer him; for they were dismayed at his presence') — is governed by the new overlay [`nivhalu-mi-panav-brothers-dismay-disclosure-scene-gen45`](#nivhalu-mi-panav-brothers-dismay-disclosure-scene-gen45). The Niphal of *bahal* is the corpus's principal sudden-terror / paralyzing-dismay lexeme (cross-corpus reach into the Psalter, Job, Isaiah, Ezekiel); chapter-singular within Genesis. The literary structural-inverse is sharp: Yehudah's just-completed Gen 44:18-34 surety-speech is one of the corpus's most extended sustained-speeches; at the disclosure-scene the brothers (and Yehudah as their de facto spokesman) collectively become the speechless-with-shock. The cycle's speech-arc inverts at the disclosure (Sternberg, Alter, Sarna).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶל־אֶחָ֛יו גְּשׁוּ־נָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וַיִּגָּ֑שׁוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֲנִי֙ יוֹסֵ֣ף אֲחִיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Yosef your brother, whom ye sold into Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ani Yosef achikhem asher-mekhartem oti Mitzraymah* — 'I am Yosef your brother, whom ye sold into Mitsrayim' — intensifies the v 3 disclosure with the explicit naming of the Gen 37 sale. The construction is governed by the new overlay [`mekhartem-oti-brothers-sale-yosef-cycle-arc`](#mekhartem-oti-brothers-sale-yosef-cycle-arc), anchoring the cycle's Qal-of-*makhar* lexical arc: Gen 37:27 (Yehudah's proposal *nimkerennu la-Yishme'elim*) → Gen 37:28 (the execution *va-yimkeru et Yosef*) → Gen 37:36 (the resale to Potifar) → Gen 45:4-5 (Yosef's verbal naming at the disclosure). The reframing about to follow (v 5: providential-purpose) does not erase the moral-weight of the original action: Yosef names the sale before he names the purpose. Westermann's reading is the canonical: the providential-reframing names a structure discoverable in retrospect but does not displace the moral-weight of the original action.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ אַל־תֵּעָ֣צְב֗וּ וְאַל־יִ֙חַר֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י הֵ֑נָּה כִּ֣י לְמִֽחְיָ֔ה שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִפְנֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And now be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for Elohim did send me before you to preserve life.

paragraphs.commentary:
The verse is the chapter's affective-and-theological centerpiece, deploying three governing entries across its three clauses.

**The emotional-discharge instruction** *al-tea'tzevu ve-al-yichar be-eineikhem* ('be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves') is governed by the new overlay [`al-teatzevu-veal-yichar-emotional-discharge-pair-gen45`](#al-teatzevu-veal-yichar-emotional-discharge-pair-gen45). The *atzav*-root carries Gen-cycle cross-references to Gen 3:16-17 (the woman's and ground's *itzavon*), Gen 5:29 (Lemekh's etymology of Noach), Gen 6:6 (YHWH's *va-yit'atzev*); the cross-cycle echo to Gen 6:6 is literarily loaded (the deity's atzav-of-heart at Gen 6:6 / Yosef's instruction-not-to-atzav at Gen 45:5). The *charah be-eineikhem* self-anger idiom parallels Gen 31:35.

**The naming of the sale** *ki-mekhartem oti hennah* echoes the v 4 *asher-mekhartem oti Mitzraymah*, completing the makhar-lexical-arc (governed by the overlay extended to vv 4 + 5).

**The providential-sending formula** *ki le-michyah shelachani Elohim lifneikhem* is the chapter's theological centerpiece — the first of three formulations (vv 5, 7, 8) governed by the new central entry [`shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle`](#shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle). The purpose-clause's load-bearing noun *michyah* is governed by the sibling central entry [`michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`](#michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun); the two entries are bidirectional central-to-central companions (the second central-to-central sibling-link in the project, after `avon-mins'so` ↔ `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword`). The noun *michyah* is rare across the HB (Gen 45:5 + Judg 6:4 + 17:10 + 2 Chr 14:13 + Ezra 9:8-9); the Ezra 9:8-9 occurrence is the post-exilic confessional prayer that lexically clusters *pleitah / she'erit / michyah* — directly echoing the Gen 45:5-7 vocabulary as the patriarchal-anchor of the remnant-tradition.

The literary-theological observation is named: von Rad reads the cycle as wisdom-narrative; Westermann reads its theology as anthropology (the providential reframing names a structure that does not displace the moral-weight of the original action); Brueggemann reads the providential reframing as the cycle's theological signature; Sternberg names it a 'subterranean theodicy'; Coats reads it as the cycle's didactic function; Alter reads it as the cycle's complex-perspectival achievement. NO Christian-soteriology of the cross is imposed; NO Joseph-as-Christ typology; NO Calvinistic compatibilism; NO project synthesis on divine providence.

The divine-name *Elohim* (anarthrous) is the cycle's standard register; governed by the existing overlay [`yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim`](#yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim), whose appliesTo extends here to cover vv 5, 7, 8, 9 — the chapter's four Elohim-occurrences, the most concentrated single-chapter Elohim-cluster since Gen 41.

paragraphs.text: כִּי־זֶ֛ה שְׁנָתַ֥יִם הָרָעָ֖ב בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְעוֹד֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־חָרִ֖ישׁ וְקָצִּֽיר׃

i18n.en: For these two years hath the famine been in the land: and there are yet five years, in which there shall be neither plowing nor harvest.

paragraphs.commentary: The *chamesh shanim* ('five years') of remaining famine is one of the chapter's three *chamesh*-instances (v 6, v 11, v 22); see commentary at v 22 on the cycle's documented fives-pattern (Gen 41:34 / 43:34 / 45:6+11+22 / 47:2).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם לָכֶ֛ם שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּלְהַחֲי֣וֹת לָכֶ֔ם לִפְלֵיטָ֖ה גְּדֹלָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Elohim sent me before you to preserve you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.

paragraphs.commentary:
Verse 7 expands the v 5 providential-sending formula to the chapter's most theologically-load-bearing articulation: the providential-purpose is named twice — *la-sum lakhem she'erit ba-aretz* ('to preserve you a remnant in the earth') and *u-le-hachayot lakhem li-pleitah gedolah* ('and to save you alive by a great deliverance'). The verse deploys three governing entries.

**The providential-sending formula** continues from v 5, governed by [`shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle`](#shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle); v 7's *va-yishlacheni Elohim lifneikhem* is the formula's second occurrence with the expanded-purpose-clause.

**The *she'erit* remnant-theological-keyword** is governed by the new central entry [`she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword`](#she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword). The lexeme is one of the HB's most-developed theological keywords; the Gen 45:7 occurrence is the patriarchal-narrative anchor of the remnant-theme that the prophets and post-exilic literature will saturate. The named scholarship apparatus: Hasel *The Remnant* 1972 (the canonical monograph), Clements *Old Testament Prophecy* 1996, Brueggemann *Theology of the OT* 1997. The cross-corpus reach includes Isa 10:20-22 (the *She'ar-Yashuv* prophecy), the Servant-Songs cluster (Isa 11:11-16, 37:31-32, 46:3), Jer 23:3 + 31:7, Ezek 9, Joel-Amos-Micah-Zephaniah, and Ezra 9:8 + 14. The Mic 7:18 great forgiveness-formula deploys the lexeme as *she'erit nachalato* ('the remnant of his inheritance').

**The *pleitah* deliverance-keyword** is governed by the new central entry [`pleitah-deliverance-escape-remnant-tradition-cross-corpus`](#pleitah-deliverance-escape-remnant-tradition-cross-corpus). The lexeme's cross-cycle echo is sharp: at Gen 32:9 Ya'aqov prays *ve-hayah ha-machaneh ha-nish'ar li-pleitah* ('the remaining camp shall be a deliverance / escape'), the patriarchal-cycle's earlier deployment of the lexeme. The Gen 32:9 prayer-for-deliverance from Esav is structurally paralleled by Yosef's declaration at Gen 45:7 that the Mitsrayim-residence IS the *pleitah gedolah* for the family. The two *pleitah*-occurrences bracket the patriarchal-cycle's brother-conflict-and-resolution structure.

The *she'erit* / *pleitah* doublet is the corpus's principal remnant-pair; the two central entries are bidirectional central-to-central companions (the project's third central-to-central sibling-link, after `avon-mins'so` ↔ `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword` and `shelachani-elohim-...` ↔ `michyah-...`). The post-exilic Ezra 9:8 *pleitah u-le-tet lanu yated... she'erit* directly echoes the Gen 45:7 lexical-cluster as the patriarchal-anchor of the post-exilic remnant-vocabulary.

The divine-name *Elohim* continues the cycle's standard register; [`yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim`](#yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim) governs.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹֽא־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִי֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְשִׂימֵ֨נִֽי לְאָ֜ב לְפַרְעֹ֗ה וּלְאָדוֹן֙ לְכָל־בֵּית֔וֹ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: So now it was not you that sent me hither, but the Elohim: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary:
Verse 8 reaches the providential-sending formula's most direct articulation: *lo-attem shelachtem oti hennah ki ha-Elohim* ('it was not you that sent me hither, but the Elohim'). The construction's contrastive-substitution is the chapter's strongest providential-statement: the verbal-subject of the sending is replaced — not the brothers (the human-agent) but ha-Elohim (the divine-agent with the marked definite article). The construction does not abolish the brothers' agency at the historical-level (the brothers did, in fact, send Yosef to Mitsrayim by selling him to the Yishme'elim); the construction names the providential-level beneath the historical-level. The reframing is not historical-erasure but theological-reframing. Named scholarship continues the v 5 + 7 cluster (von Rad, Westermann, Brueggemann, Sternberg, Coats, Alter); no Christian-soteriology of the cross is imposed; no Calvinistic compatibilism; no project synthesis. Governed by [`shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle`](#shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle); the v 8 ha-Elohim definite-article preserved as 'the Elohim'.

The three office-titles — *av le-Par'oh u-le-adon le-khol beito u-moshel be-khol eretz Mitzrayim* ('a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Mitsrayim') — name Yosef's court-position at its fullest. The first title *av le-Par'oh* is the chapter's principal interpretive-crux; governed by the new overlay [`av-le-paroh-court-advisor-title-egyptological-gen45`](#av-le-paroh-court-advisor-title-egyptological-gen45). The Egyptian-court 'father' office-title for the senior-advisor / vizier role is widely-discussed in the Egyptological literature (Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* 1959; Redford *A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph* 1970; Kitchen *Reliability of the Old Testament* 2003). The cross-corpus parallels — 2 Chr 2:13 (Huram-Abi the master-craftsman), Isa 22:21 (Elyaqim *le-av le-yoshev Yerushalayim*), Job 29:16 (Iyov *av la-evyonim*) — establish the metaphorical-'father' as a recognized HB honorific-office-title pattern.

paragraphs.text: מַהֲרוּ֮ וַעֲל֣וּ אֶל־אָבִי֒ וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ בִּנְךָ֣ יוֹסֵ֔ף שָׂמַ֧נִי אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְאָד֖וֹן לְכָל־מִצְרָ֑יִם רְדָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃

i18n.en: Haste ye, and go up to my father, and say unto him, Thus saith thy son Yosef, Elohim hath made me lord of all Mitsrayim: come down unto me, tarry not.

paragraphs.text: וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֣ בְאֶֽרֶץ־גֹּ֗שֶׁן וְהָיִ֤יתָ קָרוֹב֙ אֵלַ֔י אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֖יךָ וּבְנֵ֣י בָנֶ֑יךָ וְצֹאנְךָ֥ וּבְקָרְךָ֖ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy children, and thy children's children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:

paragraphs.commentary: *Eretz Goshen* ('the land of Goshen') is the first attestation of the chapter's principal toponym, governed by the new central entry [`goshen-egyptian-province-eastern-delta-toponym`](#goshen-egyptian-province-eastern-delta-toponym). Goshen is the named-region of the Israelite-settlement in Mitsrayim for the entire Exodus-prelude; the toponym recurs at Gen 46:28-29; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exod 8:18; 9:26. The Egyptological identifications are scholarly-debated: (a) the Wadi-Tumilat / Eastern-Delta identification (dominant; supported by the LXX *Gesem Arabias* rendering and the Roman-period Arabia-administrative-nome correlation; Kitchen, Hoffmeier); (b) the broader Eastern-Delta region (Redford, Bietak); (c) the *qsm/Qedem*-toponym identification (Redford 1970); (d) the Tell ed-Dab'a / Avaris context (Bietak). The named identifications are documented WITHOUT adjudication; no WoH ANE-archaeological synthesis is imposed. The narrative-function of Goshen is precise: a near-but-separate settlement-region where the Israelite-family is geographically-distinct from the Mitsri population, preserving the Israelite-cultic-and-genealogical distinctness through the sojourn-and-Exodus narrative-arc.

paragraphs.text: וְכִלְכַּלְתִּ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם כִּי־ע֛וֹד חָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים רָעָ֑ב פֶּן־תִּוָּרֵ֛שׁ אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵֽיתְךָ֖ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: and there will I nourish thee; for there are yet five years of famine; lest thou come to poverty, thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ve-khilkalti otkha sham* — 'and there will I nourish thee' — is governed by the new overlay [`kalkel-yosef-sustenance-promise-gen45-46-47-50`](#kalkel-yosef-sustenance-promise-gen45-46-47-50). The Pilpel of *kul* names the cycle's three-fold sustenance-promise arc: Gen 45:11 (here, the promise), Gen 47:12 (the fulfilment: *va-yekhalkel Yosef et-aviv ve-et-echav*), Gen 50:21 (the post-Ya'aqov-death repetition: *anokhi achalkel etkhem*). Cross-corpus reach into 2 Sam 19:33-34 (Barzilai sustaining David), 1 Kgs 4:7 (Shelomoh's twelve officers), 1 Kgs 17:4 + 9 (Eliyahu sustained at Kerit and Tzarphat), 1 Kgs 18:4 + 13 (Obadyah sustaining the prophets). The lexeme is the corpus's principal sustenance-and-support verb; promotion-seed noted.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֤ה עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ רֹא֔וֹת וְעֵינֵ֖י אָחִ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין כִּי־פִ֖י הַֽמְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Binyamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ki fi ha-medabber aleikhem* ('that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you') is the chapter's explicit literary-reversal of Gen 42:23's *ki ha-melitz beinotam* ('for there was an interpreter between them'). The cycle's speech-mediation structure inverts: at Gen 42:23 the institutional court-interpreter mediated between Yosef and the brothers, allowing the brothers' unguarded Hebrew-confession (vv 21-22) to be overheard by the *shallit* without their knowledge; at Gen 45:12 the interpreter-mediation is dispensed-with, and the marked emphasis falls on Yosef's *peh* (mouth) speaking directly in Hebrew. Governed by the new overlay [`fi-ha-medabber-aleikhem-direct-speech-reversal-melitz-gen45`](#fi-ha-medabber-aleikhem-direct-speech-reversal-melitz-gen45); SIBLING bidirectional cross-reference to the existing overlay [`melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42`](#melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42). The pair governs the cycle's signature mediated-speech / direct-speech reversal (Alter, Sternberg, Fokkelman, Sarna).

paragraphs.text: וְהִגַּדְתֶּ֣ם לְאָבִ֗י אֶת־כָּל־כְּבוֹדִי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְאִיתֶ֑ם וּמִֽהַרְתֶּ֛ם וְהוֹרַדְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־אָבִ֖י הֵֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Mitsrayim, and of all that ye have seen; and ye shall haste and bring down my father hither.

paragraphs.commentary: *Kol kevodi be-Mitzrayim* ('all my glory in Mitsrayim') deploys *kavod* in the court-office-honor register, governed by the new overlay [`kavod-court-office-honor-yosef-egyptian-glory-gen45`](#kavod-court-office-honor-yosef-egyptian-glory-gen45). The register is distinct from the divine-glory-of-YHWH cluster (Exod 16, 24, 33, 40; Lev 9; Isa 6; Ezek 1, 10, 43) that dominates the lexeme's theological-load-bearing occurrences. Cross-corpus parallels in the court-honor register: Esth 1:4 (Achashverosh's *kevod malkhuto*); Esth 5:11 (Haman's *kevod oshro*); Isa 22:18 (Shevna's *merkevot kevodkha*). The chapter's credentialing-function is precise: the reported *kavod* is part of what will eventually persuade Ya'aqov to believe the impossible news (cf. v 27 *va-techi ruach* on seeing the wagons).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפֹּ֛ל עַל־צַוְּארֵ֥י בִנְיָמִֽן־אָחִ֖יו וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן בָּכָ֖ה עַל־צַוָּארָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he fell upon his brother Binyamin's neck, and wept; and Binyamin wept upon his neck.

paragraphs.commentary:
The reunion-embrace formula *va-yippol al-tzavarav + va-yevk* ('fell upon his neck and wept') is the corpus's signature reunion-formula, governed by the new overlay [`va-yippol-al-tzavarav-reunion-embrace-formula-gen45`](#va-yippol-al-tzavarav-reunion-embrace-formula-gen45). The Genesis-internal cluster: Gen 33:4 (Esav's reunion-embrace with Ya'aqov, famously marked by the *puncta extraordinaria* over *va-yishshakehu*); Gen 45:14-15 (here); Gen 46:29 (Yosef's reunion-embrace with Ya'aqov on the descent, *va-yevk al tzavarav od* — 'wept on his neck a good while'). The triple-deployment Gen 33:4 → 45:14-15 → 46:29 is one of the corpus's most-cited reunion-formula clusters (Alter, Sternberg, Sarna).

The v 14 embrace is mutual and reciprocal — both subjects fall on each other's neck and weep — naming Binyamin specifically as the direct-brother of the Rachel-side, the only one Yosef has had no reason to be estranged from. The chapter-internal contrast with v 15 (where the brothers' reciprocity is muted) is part of the chapter's literary signature for the unresolved Gen 37 guilt-residue.

paragraphs.text: וַיְנַשֵּׁ֥ק לְכָל־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֵּ֣בְךְּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן דִּבְּר֥וּ אֶחָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.

paragraphs.commentary: Verse 15 completes the chapter-internal embrace-pair (v 14 Yosef-Binyamin; v 15 Yosef-brothers), with the marked asymmetry: Yosef kisses the brothers and weeps upon them, but the text does not record the brothers' reciprocity. The contrast with v 14 (where Binyamin reciprocates fully) is named literary observation: the brothers' Gen 37 guilt-residue is not yet discharged, and only after Yosef's outward affection does *dibberu echav itto* ('his brethren talked with him') record speech finally resuming. The cycle's reconciliation is graduated. The *va-yenashek* ('he kissed') deploys the Piel of *nashaq* in the cycle's reunion-kiss register; cross-cycle echoes to Gen 27:26-27 (Yitzchaq's blessing-kiss), Gen 29:11+13 (Ya'aqov-Rachel, Lavan-Ya'aqov), Gen 31:28+55 (Lavan's departure-kiss), Gen 33:4 (Esav's puncta-marked kiss), Gen 48:10 (Ya'aqov's blessing-kiss of Yosef's sons), Gen 50:1 (Yosef's death-kiss of Ya'aqov) — the corpus-wide kiss-vocabulary is reserved for a future central treatment; chapter-specific deployment is commentary-only here.

paragraphs.text: וְהַקֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמַ֗ע בֵּ֤ית פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֖אוּ אֲחֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּבְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And the report thereof was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, Yosef's brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֱמֹ֥ר אֶל־אַחֶ֖יךָ זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ טַֽעֲנוּ֙ אֶת־בְּעִ֣ירְכֶ֔ם וּלְכוּ־בֹ֖אוּ אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto Yosef, Say unto thy brethren, This do ye: lade your beasts, and go, get you unto the land of Kena'an;

paragraphs.text: וּקְח֧וּ אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֛ם וְאֶת־בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם וּבֹ֣אוּ אֵלָ֑י וְאֶתְּנָ֣ה לָכֶ֗ם אֶת־טוּב֙ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאִכְל֖וּ אֶת־חֵ֥לֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: and take your father and your households, and come unto me: and I will give you the good of the land of Mitsrayim, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.

paragraphs.commentary: *Chelev ha-aretz* ('the fat of the land') deploys the noun *chelev* in the metaphorical 'best/richest part' register, governed by the new overlay [`chelev-ha-aretz-best-of-the-land-pharaoh-grant-gen45`](#chelev-ha-aretz-best-of-the-land-pharaoh-grant-gen45). The register is distinct from the technical Levitical sacrificial-fat sense (Lev 3:14-17; 7:23-25, the *kol chelev ve-khol dam lo tochelu* prohibition); the metaphorical-extension recurs at Num 18:12 (the priestly grant), Deut 32:14 (Song of Mosheh), Ps 81:17, Ps 147:14 (*chelev chittim*). The Pharaoh-grant context is the corpus's only deployment of the unspecified *chelev ha-aretz* phrase (the other metaphorical occurrences specify the agricultural-product: *chelev chittah*, *chelev yitzhar*); the construction names the totality of the land's bounty (Sarna).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֥ה צֻוֵּ֖יתָה זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ קְחוּ־לָכֶם֩ מֵאֶ֨רֶץ מִצְרַ֜יִם עֲגָל֗וֹת לְטַפְּכֶם֙ וְלִנְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם וּנְשָׂאתֶ֥ם אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֖ם וּבָאתֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Now thou art commanded, this do ye: take you wagons out of the land of Mitsrayim for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

paragraphs.commentary: *Agalot* ('wagons') is the chapter's principal material-token; governed by the new overlay [`agalot-pharaoh-issue-wagons-yosef-cycle-gen45`](#agalot-pharaoh-issue-wagons-yosef-cycle-gen45). The lexeme recurs three times in the chapter — v 19 (Pharaoh's instruction), v 21 (the fulfilment), v 27 (Ya'aqov's seeing) — and serves as the credentialing-token of the brothers' impossible report. Cross-corpus reach: Num 7:3 + 6-8 (the Mishkan-transport wagons), 1 Sam 6:7-14 (the Pelishtim's ark-return wagon), 2 Sam 6:3 (Uzzah's ill-fated ark-transport), Isa 5:18 (the cart-rope idiom), Amos 2:13 (the cart full of sheaves). Egyptological context: the New Kingdom royal-issue wagons documented by Vergote, Redford, Kitchen; the Pharaoh-grant is historically-plausible Egyptian-court practice.

paragraphs.text: וְעֵ֣ינְכֶ֔ם אַל־תָּחֹ֖ס עַל־כְּלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּי־ט֛וּב כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לָכֶ֥ם הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: Also regard not your stuff; for the good of all the land of Mitsrayim is yours.

paragraphs.commentary: *Al tachos al keleikhem* ('regard not your stuff') deploys the *chus al* construction in its rare positive-context register (the not-sparing is encouraged-by-context-of-abundance rather than required-by-judicial-justice), governed by the new central entry [`chus-al-spare-regard-with-pity-cross-corpus-keyword`](#chus-al-spare-regard-with-pity-cross-corpus-keyword). The lexeme is one of the corpus's principal mercy/pity-formulae, with extensive cross-corpus reach: the Deuteronomic eye-shall-not-spare formulae (Deut 7:16; 13:9; 19:13, 21; 25:12), Samuel (1 Sam 24:11 David's sparing of Sha'ul), the prophets (Isa 13:18, Jer 13:14 + 21:7, Ezekielian saturation), the Twelve (Joel 2:17 priestly intercession; Jonah 4:10-11 the great mercy-question). The Gen 45:20 deployment's contextual-irony: the same construction that the Deuteronomic formulae deploy for the prohibition-of-mercy-in-judgment is here deployed for the prohibition-of-clinging-in-abundance.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֥ם יוֹסֵ֛ף עֲגָל֖וֹת עַל־פִּ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֛ם צֵדָ֖ה לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Yisra'el did so: and Yosef gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.

paragraphs.text: לְכֻלָּ֥ם נָתַ֛ן לָאִ֖ישׁ חֲלִפ֣וֹת שְׂמָלֹ֑ת וּלְבִנְיָמִ֤ן נָתַן֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְחָמֵ֖שׁ חֲלִפֹ֥ת שְׂמָלֹֽת׃

i18n.en: To all of them he gave each man changes of raiment; but to Binyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment.

paragraphs.commentary: *Chamesh chalifot semalot* ('five changes of raiment') governs both the chapter-internal Binyamin-asymmetry-gift and the cycle's broader *chamesh*-fives-pattern. The new overlay [`chamesh-chalifot-semalot-fives-pattern-gen45`](#chamesh-chalifot-semalot-fives-pattern-gen45) anchors the chapter's fives-pattern observation across the cycle: Gen 41:34 (*chimmesh*, the Piel administrative-verb governed by [`chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41`](#chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41)); Gen 43:34 (*chamesh yadot*, the fivefold-portion governed by [`chamesh-yadot-fivefold-portion-gen43`](#chamesh-yadot-fivefold-portion-gen43)); Gen 45:6, 11 (five famine-years); Gen 45:22 (here); Gen 47:2 (five brothers Yosef presents to Pharaoh). The Binyamin-asymmetry sub-pattern (Gen 43:34 + Gen 45:22) is structurally significant: Binyamin twice receives five-times what the other brothers receive (Alter, Sarna, Sternberg). The *chalifot semalot* gift-formula's cross-corpus parallels: Judg 14:12-13, 19 (the Shimshon-riddle-wager *sheloshim chalifot begadim*); 2 Kgs 5:5 + 22-23 (Na'aman's *eser chalifot begadim* to Elisha + Gechazi's seizure of two).

paragraphs.text: וּלְאָבִ֞יו שָׁלַ֤ח כְּזֹאת֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה חֲמֹרִ֔ים נֹשְׂאִ֖ים מִטּ֣וּב מִצְרָ֑יִם וְעֶ֣שֶׂר אֲתֹנֹ֡ת נֹֽ֠שְׂאֹת בָּ֣ר וָלֶ֧חֶם וּמָז֛וֹן לְאָבִ֖יו לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And to his father he sent after this manner ten asses laden with the good things of Mitsrayim, and ten she-asses laden with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.

paragraphs.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַֽל־תִּרְגְּז֖וּ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

i18n.en: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said unto them, See that ye fall not out by the way.

paragraphs.commentary: *Al tirgezu ba-derekh* is one of the chapter's principal philological-cruxes; governed by the new overlay [`al-tirgezu-ba-derekh-philological-crux-gen45`](#al-tirgezu-ba-derekh-philological-crux-gen45). The verb *ragaz* carries a wide semantic-range that produces four principal readings: (i) the agitation/trembling sense (the standard physical-or-emotional-agitation register, Exod 15:14, Deut 2:25, etc.); (ii) the affective be-disturbed sense (2 Sam 19:1, Ps 4:5); (iii) the conflict / quarrel sense (the rabbinic-tradition reading, b. Ta'an. 10b, Rashi: *al tariv* 'do not quarrel'); (iv) the fear / be-alarmed sense (Saadia). The KJV/ASV 'see that ye fall not out by the way' preserves the quarrel-reading (the dominant Jewish-tradition + KJV/ASV consensus); NJPS 'do not be quarrelsome'; Alter 'do not be troubled along the way'. The crux is documented in named scholarship (Rashi citing multiple readings, Targum Onqelos *la-titnatzun be-orcha*, modern HALOT / BDB).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲבִיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And they went up out of Mitsrayim, and came into the land of Kena'an unto Ya'aqov their father.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ ל֜וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר ע֚וֹד יוֹסֵ֣ף חַ֔י וְכִֽי־ה֥וּא מֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֣פָג לִבּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י לֹא־הֶאֱמִ֖ין לָהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And they told him, saying, Yosef is yet alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Mitsrayim. And his heart fainted, for he believed them not.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yafag libbo* ('his heart fainted') deploys the rare Qal of *pug* 'grow numb, faint, cease', governed by the new overlay [`va-yafag-libbo-heart-grew-numb-rare-form-gen45`](#va-yafag-libbo-heart-grew-numb-rare-form-gen45). The construction is chapter-singular within Genesis and near-singular within the HB: the only other Qal-stem occurrence is Ps 77:3 (*niggrah ve-lo tafug*, the de profundis lament's not-ceasing); Hab 1:4 *tafug torah* is the related deployment with debated form-analysis. The construction is a deliberate-marked-rare-form for Ya'aqov's emotional-physiological-collapse on hearing the impossible news. The v 26 collapse is structurally paired with the immediately-following v 27 *va-techi ruach* (the spirit-revival); the lexical pairing *va-yafag libbo* / *va-techi ruach* maps the affective-collapse / revival across the two-verse pivot.

The brothers' announcement *od Yosef chai* ('Yosef is yet alive') echoes Yosef's own v 3 *ani Yosef ha-od avi chai* and Ya'aqov's v 28 *od Yosef beni chai* — completing the chapter's three-part *od-Yosef-chai* refrain (Alter, Sternberg, Westermann).

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֣ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹסֵף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֲגָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח יוֹסֵ֖ף לָשֵׂ֣את אֹת֑וֹ וַתְּחִ֕י ר֖וּחַ יַעֲקֹ֥ב אֲבִיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And they told him all the words of Yosef, which he had said unto them: and when he saw the wagons which Yosef had sent to carry him, the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived:

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-techi ruach Ya'aqov avihem* ('the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived') closes the chapter's chayah-keyword arc, governed by the new overlay [`va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45`](#va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45). The chapter-internal chayah-arc traces: v 5 *le-michyah* (providential-purpose; the rare *michyah* noun governed by the central [`michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`](#michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun)); v 7 *u-le-hachayot* (expanded-providential-purpose, the Hiphil-infinitive); v 27 *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov* (fulfilment-in-the-father's-spirit-revival). The chapter is structurally a chayah-narrative: the preservation-of-life-as-providential-purpose tracks all the way to the father's literal revival. Cross-corpus spirit-revival construction: Judg 15:19 (Shimshon's *va-tashav rucho va-yechi*), 1 Sam 30:12 (the Mitsri-servant David finds: *va-tashav rucho elav*). The narrative-architecture is precise: the wagons serve as the visual-evidence (*va-yare et ha-agalot*) that turns Ya'aqov from disbelief (v 26 *va-yafag libbo*) to revival (v 27 *va-techi ruach*) — the Pharaoh-issue material-tokens function as the chapter's credentialing-proof.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֛ב עוֹד־יוֹסֵ֥ף בְּנִ֖י חָ֑י אֵֽלְכָ֥ה וְאֶרְאֶ֖נּוּ בְּטֶ֥רֶם אָמֽוּת׃

i18n.en: and Yisra'el said, It is enough; Yosef my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's narrative-pivot from *Ya'aqov* (vv 25, 27 twice) to *Yisra'el* (v 28) is a marked literary observation, governed by the new overlay [`yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-yosef-cycle-acceptance-v28`](#yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-yosef-cycle-acceptance-v28). The patriarch's acceptance-of-the-news and his determination-to-go is voiced under the Yisra'el-name (the covenantal-name granted at Gen 32:29 + 35:10, governed by the existing overlays [`yisrael-name-aetiology-sarah-im-elohim`](#yisrael-name-aetiology-sarah-im-elohim) and [`yisrael-second-renaming-beit-el-p-doublet`](#yisrael-second-renaming-beit-el-p-doublet)), not the Ya'aqov-name (the patriarchal-aetiology name from Gen 25:26). The chapter-internal pivot — from grief-stricken-and-disbelieving Ya'aqov (vv 25-27) to determined-and-acting Yisra'el (v 28) — is documented across mainstream commentary (von Rad, Sarna, Alter, Brueggemann, Westermann); the cycle's broader Ya'aqov/Yisra'el alternation continues across Gen 46:1-2 + 47:27-31 + 48:2 + 49:1-2 and is potentially a future cycle-wide central-candidate. The closing *od Yosef beni chai* ('Yosef my son is yet alive') completes the chapter's three-part *od-Yosef-chai* refrain (v 3 Yosef's self-disclosure; v 26 the brothers' announcement; v 28 the patriarch's acceptance).
